title: Symmetric debris requires a late return branch in the ASASSN-14ko delay example
abstract: We test a shared-delay example for ASASSN-14ko under symmetric tidal stripping and Newtonian ballistic return. Equal debris mass on either side of the core orbital energy requires an exact paired return-time relation. For the published synthetic 70-90-day pulse and a 108.44-day core period, the late branch spans 134.17-201.71 days and has equal mass. Delaying the early branch by 5.9558 days moves the late branch 10.28-28.59 days earlier at fixed core period. We prove that an exact time translation of a full continuous symmetric debris distribution cannot preserve energy symmetry about any centre. We give a four-quantile period estimator that removes a common additive time delay and test its limits. It recovers exact symmetric examples, including two tails with a gap. However, narrow energy ranges make it unstable, and a selected 2-percent quadratic energy distortion biases a 108.44-day period to 95.87 or 124.76 days. These are model results, not observed late branches or a measurement of orbital decay. The test requires a complete return tracer and validated energy symmetry, neither of which is established for ASASSN-14ko.

display.caption: A symmetric late branch for the published synthetic early pulse, its opposite timing change, and noise sensitivity of a conditional period estimator. No telescope measurements are plotted.
